sources.citation: Hale, Herbert M. & Norman B. Tindale. 1933-34. Aborigines of Princess Charlotte Bay, North Queensland. Records of the South Australian Museum 5(1):63-116, 5(2):117-172. (LANGUAGE section pp.158-159; comparative vocabulary with a Mutumui = Barrow Point/Eibole column from p.160)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a notation remark, p.158: 'A stress accent is placed at the beginning of the emphasized syllable.' In the Mutumui (Barrow Point) vocabulary column the mark is applied only sporadically and falls on different syllables (p.160: 'yorlpan, 'armun, 'workan with initial stress; walan'gar, awul'war with non-initial stress; most words unmarked). No rule for where stress falls is stated.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. Publications list and Curriculum Vitae, pages.ucsd.edu/~jhaviland (Publications/; Publications/ directory listing incl. FogBook/ and FieldNOtes/)
sources.note: Confirms Haviland published no grammar/sketch/phonology of Barrow Point: only the 1998 memoir and the 2006 lexicography chapter; CV lists fieldwork on Barrow Point language 1980-1992 ('Uwu I:bu:linnganh') and an unpublished 'Barrow Point Wordlist' (computer listings, 1982-1989). FieldNOtes/ directory holds only 1966-68 Chiapas/Suriname notes.

Third-hand: says Barrow Point had fricatives /ð/ and /ɣ/ that 'usually developed from *t̪ and *k, respectively, when preceded by a stressed long vowel, which then shortened', citing Dixon 2002. No statement of synchronic stress placement.

sources.citation: Flinders, Johnny & Peter Sutton. 2025. Cardinal direction enclitics in the Flinders Island Language, Cape York Peninsula. In Projecting Voices (ANU Press), ch. 12. DOI 10.22459/PV.2025.12
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Flinders Island language only (one remark: FI maleerra 'mast' has primary stress on V2); nothing on Barrow Point.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 2006. Documenting lexical knowledge. In J. Gippert, N. Himmelmann & U. Mosel (eds), Essentials of Language Documentation, 129-162. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter; read in the Spanish version: Haviland, 'La documentacion del conocimiento lexico', ch. 6 of Haviland & Flores Farfan (coords.) 2007, Bases de la documentacion linguistica, Mexico: INALI (scanned text layer).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Barrow Point elicitation with Roger Hart is used as a lexicographic example (working through Guugu Yimithirr); no phonology, no transcription conventions for stress.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2001. Where have all the onsets gone? Initial consonant loss in Australian Aboriginal languages. In Simpson et al. (eds), Forty Years On: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 481-492. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 512.

sources.note: Appendix table lists 'Barrow Point Lg.' as an initial-dropping language of the 'sporadic' type, sourced to 'Alpher (1976) (pers. comm. from John Haviland via Bruce Rigsby)'; no statement about Barrow Point stress placement.

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. with Roger Hart. 1998. Old Man Fog and the Last Aborigines of Barrow Point. Washington DC: Smithsonian Institution Press. (author-posted scans: Front matter/Introduction pp. xv-xviii; Afterward, Glossary, Notes, Bibliography, Index)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic memoir; Barrow Point words in bold italics, no pronunciation guide. Note 42 (p.199) remarks only that variant place-name spellings 'attest to a complex vowel system in the Barrow Point language whose proper reconstruction is probably now impossible.'

sources.citation: Haviland, John B. 1991. 'That was the last time I seen them, and no more': voices through time in Australian Aboriginal autobiography. American Ethnologist 18(2):331-361.
